item.title: Jake Whisenant, Who Raced Up Yosemite’s El Capitan at Record Speed, Dies in a Fall
item.description: Authorities in California said he died in a climbing accident. He set a record in 2024 for climbing El Capitan’s Lurking Fear route in under three hours.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Regalado
item.media:credit: Loren Elliott for The New York Times
item.media:description: El Capitan in Yosemite National Park last year. Jake Whisenant set a speed record on its Lurking Fear route in 2024.

item.title: Californians Criticize Federal Efforts to Control the State’s Coast

item.media:description: The coastline in Pacifica, Calif.

item.title: North Carolina G.O.P. Picks Replacement for Candidate Plagued by Scandal

item.title: Homeland Security Intensifies Pursuit of Noncitizens on Voter Rolls
item.description: Immigrants who said they inadvertently registered to vote while obtaining or renewing driver’s licenses are increasingly facing deportation under the Trump administration.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo, Nick Corasaniti and Hamed Aleaziz
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: In the past, the Homeland Security Department has not aggressively tried to deport the relatively small number of noncitizens who unlawfully registered to vote.

item.title: Hegseth Renames Base for Lindsey Graham

item.title: Trump Concedes There Was ‘Some Contractor Error’ in Reflecting Pool Renovations
item.description: The president had insisted for weeks that the landmarks’ algae-stained waters and peeling lining were the fault of vandals, not the project itself.
item.dc:creator: David A. Fahrenthold

item.media:description: Investigators concluded that botched work by a contractor, not vandalism, had caused the Reflecting Pool’s recent problems.

item.title: One Source of Paxton’s Wealth: A Cell Tower at a Hospital He Knew Well

item.title: Minnesota’s Democratic Senate Primary Pits Angie Craig Against Peggy Flanagan
item.description: The Senate primary race in Minnesota will be the latest test of left-wing energy in the party, in a state that was convulsed by the Trump administration’s deadly immigration crackdown this winter.
item.dc:creator: Ernesto Londoño and Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Ellen Schmidt/Associated Press
item.media:description: Ms. Flanagan, third from left, has been backed by Minnesota Democrats and national progressives including, from left, Senator Tina Smith, Senator Bernie Sanders, Representative Ilhan Omar and Keith Ellison, the Minnesota attorney general.

item.title: The Campaign Tactics Helping Progressives Win Primaries Ahead of the 2026 Midterms
item.description: Progressives are being outspent and are receiving little support from the Democratic Party. Their tactics show a different way to succeed.
item.dc:creator: Kellen Browning, Tim Balk and Dan Simmons
item.media:credit: Jenn Ackerman for The New York Times
item.media:description: The campaign of Francesca Hong, a democratic socialist running for governor of Wisconsin, has recruited about 7,000 volunteers, knocked on hundreds of thousands of doors and hosted roughly 500 canvassing events.
